meta.theme: a teacher's failed year of manufactured obstacles used to separate effort from the operation it is spent on: a difficulty pays only where it makes the learner perform the judgement the subject consists of, so difficulty is the symptom of a transferred decision rather than the ingredient, and neither the amount of effort nor the volume of complaint measures it

meta.reviewer_notes: The narrative is written so that the failed year supplies counter-examples in both directions: the most resented change is one the author keeps, and the change nobody noticed is the one that worked. Three rival readings — effort as the ingredient, tolerance of discomfort as the variable, and any transfer of work as sufficient — each own one option in all four questions.

quality.adversarial_review: Three complete rivals run beside the author's account through all four questions. The first is effort as the active ingredient: struggle is what teaches, so the failed year failed by degree. It holds the hardest-working-courses strengthener, the comparative in the detail item, the claim that an unnoticed difficulty cannot be working, and the main idea that raises what a course asks. It dies twice over: the visitor 'asked for less work than I did, not more', and the change that worked best 'takes twenty seconds and costs nothing' and was never noticed. The second is tolerance of discomfort: learners mistake ease for progress, so the teacher's task is to make them bear the feeling. It dies on 'Nobody in that room looked uncomfortable; they argued', and on the closing observation that complaint carries no information in either direction. The third, and the live rival, is any transfer of work: whatever the teacher stops doing, the class must do, so the lecturer should do less. It survives longest because the two changes the author keeps are transfers, and it dies on the dozen that were also transfers and returned nothing — a decoded page, a survived deadline, a tolerated neighbour — and on the sentence that names the restriction: none of them 'made anybody do the thing the course existed to teach'. The detail item is decided by 'the only difference between her hour and mine was where in it she did that', which refutes the reading that she withheld the method altogether.

passage.title: The Year I Made It Harder

paragraphs.text: A visiting lecturer took one of my classes for an hour in my second year of teaching and ruined the twelve months that followed. The material was the ordinary first-year fare, sampling and error, and I had taught it the same way for four terms: state the principle, work an example, set a problem resembling it. She did something simpler. She put a question on the screen, gave the room four minutes, and made every student write down an answer before she said anything at all. Most of the answers were wrong. She then showed the working in full, exactly as I would have shown it, and the only difference between her hour and mine was where in it she did that. She asked for less work than I did, not more. Nobody in that room looked uncomfortable; they argued. Two months later, on that topic alone, they answered better than any group I had taught.

I drew the obvious conclusion, and drew it far too widely. If struggle was what had done the work, my course had been too comfortable, and over the following year I made it harder in every way I could devise. I set readings a level above the class. I moved deadlines without notice. I stopped handing out slides. I gave out photocopies of photocopies, on the theory that a page which resists being read gets read properly. I changed the seating every week so that nobody could depend on a neighbour. By any measure I could apply it was a much harder course, and the class said so at length. The marks fell. The ratings fell further.

Two of the changes survived the audit I made afterwards, and they are not the two anyone would pick. The first was the removal of the slides, which the class resented more than anything else I did and which I would do again: deciding which part of an hour is worth writing down is not an obstacle placed in front of the subject, it is a piece of the subject, and a working statistician spends most of the day doing it. The second nobody noticed at all. Halfway through the year I had begun asking the room to predict the result of each worked example before I ran it, which takes twenty seconds and costs nothing, and the questions I was asked afterwards were sharper than any I had had before. The rest were inert. A page that resists being read is decoded, not understood; a deadline moved without notice is survived; a stranger in the next seat is tolerated. Every one of them raised the effort the course demanded, and none of them made anybody do the thing the course existed to teach.

What the visitor had done, I saw eventually, was not to make the hour harder but to move one decision. The moment of judgement had been mine and she made it theirs, and the difficulty was simply what that felt like from inside. Difficulty is the symptom and not the medicine, which is why make it harder is not the instruction the evidence supports, and why a dozen obstacles could all be harder while only two were worth anything. It is also why complaint tells you nothing: the change I would keep was the most resented of them all, and the change that worked best was never noticed. The diagnostic question is not how much effort a task costs. It is what the student is doing while spending it, and whether they will have to do that unaided later.

questions.target_mistake: strengthening a rival account of the failed year — that effort is the ingredient, that discomfort must be tolerated, or that any work moved to the class pays — instead of the author's, which turns on what the effort is spent doing
questions.prediction_target: The learner should first name the variable the author says is doing the work — whether the task requires the judgement the subject consists of — and predict a strengthener that varies that while holding the amount of effort fixed.
questions.stem: Which of the following, if true, would most strengthen the author's explanation of why most of his changes made no difference?

options.A: Courses whose students report working hardest over the year are those whose students score highest in the final examinations.
options.B: Two classes given tasks of equal length gained more where the task made them commit to a verdict, and no more where it merely took longer.
options.C: Students who are warned in advance that a course will feel unpleasant before it becomes useful stay with it longer and finish it better.
options.D: Classes whose teachers demonstrate fewer of the steps at the board outperform those whose teachers demonstrate every step.

explanation.expert_notice: The explanation is causal and its variable is named in one clause at the end of the third paragraph: every obstacle 'raised the effort the course demanded, and none of them made anybody do the thing the course existed to teach'. Effort is held constant in the author's own comparison; what varies is the operation.
explanation.correct_reasoning: The correct option reports an outcome in which that variable moves and nothing else does. Matching the two tasks for length removes the rival explanation that the good cases simply cost more, and the second half, finding no gain where the extra time bought no commitment, rules out duration as the active ingredient. This is evidence about the mechanism rather than about the subject's conclusion, which is what a strengthen question asks for.
explanation.question_type_note: A strengthen question is about the join between evidence and conclusion. Name the variable the author says is doing the work, then take the option that moves that variable while holding the others still.
explanation.reading_habit: Write the author's claim as 'it worked because of X, not because of Y'. A strengthener must separate X from Y; an option that raises both at once leaves the argument exactly where it was.

distractors.why_wrong: This supports the account the passage was written to abandon, in which effort itself is the ingredient. The author's own year is the counter-example: it was 'a much harder course' by every measure he could apply, and the marks fell. A finding that hard-working cohorts score well leaves open why his did not.
distractors.seductive_element: It sounds like the research the author says he was following, and it points in the direction the whole first paragraph seems to be going.

distractors.why_wrong: It strengthens a different explanation, that the trouble was the students' tolerance of discomfort. The passage closes that off from both ends: the visiting lecturer's students were not uncomfortable at all, and the change that worked best in the failed year was the one nobody noticed.
distractors.seductive_element: The falling ratings and the class complaining at length put student feeling in the reader's mind as the thing that went wrong.

distractors.why_wrong: Every account on offer predicts this, the author's included, so it separates none of them. It is also consistent with the failed year, in which the lecturer demonstrated less in several ways and taught less; what the author needs supported is the restriction on which transfers pay, and this option is silent about it.
distractors.seductive_element: It is the near-tie: the two changes the author keeps are both things he stopped doing, so an option about a teacher doing less looks like his own conclusion.

questions.target_mistake: remembering the visiting lecturer's hour as a withholding of help, when the passage states that she gave the same working and differed only in when
questions.stem: According to the passage, what distinguished the visiting lecturer's hour from the author's usual practice was that she

options.A: asked the class for a greater quantity of work than he had been in the habit of asking
options.B: left the class uneasy enough to attend to the material more closely than they had before
options.C: withheld the method altogether and left the class to arrive at it without her help
options.D: required every student to commit to an answer before any method had been shown

explanation.expert_notice: The paragraph describes her hour and then removes every candidate difference in turn: she 'showed the working in full, exactly as I would have shown it', 'asked for less work than I did, not more', and her room was not uncomfortable. What is left is one sentence: 'the only difference between her hour and mine was where in it she did that.'
explanation.correct_reasoning: The correct option is that remaining difference stated from the students' side. They had to produce an answer and a number before anything was explained, so the judgement came first and the method afterwards. The author's own practice put the same method first and the judgement second, which is why he calls it a move of one decision rather than an increase in difficulty.
explanation.question_type_note: When a passage names a difference between two cases, the detail question is answered from the sentence that isolates it. Expect decoys built from the other features of the same episode, which the passage has explicitly equalised.
explanation.reading_habit: Where an author says two things differed 'only' in something, treat every other feature as ruled out. Those ruled-out features are exactly what the wrong options will be made of.

distractors.why_wrong: The passage states the comparison in the opposite direction: 'She asked for less work than I did, not more.' The reader who chooses this has supplied the quantity that the research the author was following seemed to require.
distractors.seductive_element: The whole passage is about difficulty, and a demand for more work is what difficulty is assumed to mean.

distractors.why_wrong: The passage denies it in the same paragraph: 'Nobody in that room looked uncomfortable; they argued.' Discomfort is what the author later manufactured for a year, with results that the fourth paragraph uses to show that feeling is not the measure.
distractors.seductive_element: Everyone knows the maxim that learning ought to feel uncomfortable, and the option supplies it where the passage has deliberately left it out.

distractors.why_wrong: She did withhold the method, but only until the answers were down; the passage then says she 'showed the working in full, exactly as I would have shown it'. A reading on which the class was left to find the method unaided loses the sentence that makes the episode an argument about timing.
distractors.seductive_element: It is the near-tie, and it matches the popular picture of discovery teaching, in which the teacher's silence is the whole method.

questions.target_mistake: treating what a class feels — resentment, or the absence of any felt effort — as evidence about whether a difficulty was the productive kind
questions.prediction_target: The learner should be able to say beforehand: the passage has one case that was hated and kept and one that was unnoticed and effective, so whatever the class felt cannot be the measure.
questions.stem: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?

options.A: How strongly a class objects to a change is a poor guide to whether the change was worth making.
options.B: A difficulty that a class does not notice is unlikely to be doing very much work on its behalf.
options.C: A class persuaded in advance to expect discomfort would have taken that year of changes better than this one did.
options.D: An hour in which the lecturer does less of the work will teach more than an hour in which he does more.

explanation.expert_notice: The fourth paragraph supplies both halves of the case in one sentence: 'the change I would keep was the most resented of them all, and the change that worked best was never noticed.' One case where objection accompanied a good change, one where its absence accompanied another.
explanation.correct_reasoning: The correct option follows from that pair. If a valuable change drew the loudest objection and another drew none, the level of objection varies independently of the value, so a teacher who reads it as a signal will be misled in either direction. The passage does not say that objection is a good sign or a bad one, which is exactly why it cannot be used as a guide.
explanation.question_type_note: When a passage supplies counter-examples in both directions, the inference is usually that the variable in question is uninformative — not that it points the other way.
explanation.reading_habit: Collect the author's examples before reading the options and ask what they have in common. Two cases that disagree about a signal are a statement that the signal is empty.

distractors.why_wrong: The passage's best case is the opposite. The prediction habit 'takes twenty seconds and costs nothing' and was never noticed, and the questions that followed it were sharper than any the author had been asked. Felt effort accompanies difficulty without measuring it.
distractors.seductive_element: It preserves the intuition the author began with, that the work must be felt to be doing anything, and the passage never states the denial in so many words.

distractors.why_wrong: Nothing in the passage bears on what preparation would have done, and the diagnosis given for the rest is not that the class refused them but that they were inert: a decoded page, a survived deadline, a tolerated neighbour. Persuading a class to accept an empty obstacle would not fill it.
distractors.seductive_element: The falling ratings make the class's attitude look like the obstacle, and the remedy of managing expectations is a familiar one.

distractors.why_wrong: The failed year is a list of things the lecturer stopped doing, and it taught less. The passage keeps a restriction that this option drops: the transfer has to put the student to work on the judgement the subject consists of, which the photocopies and the seating plan did not.
distractors.seductive_element: Both of the changes the author defends are things he stopped doing, so the general rule appears to be the lesson of his own audit.

questions.target_mistake: reading a narrative about a failed year as a recantation of difficulty, or as an endorsement of difficulty that merely went too far
questions.prediction_target: Before the options the learner should be able to say: the effort is not what pays; what pays is whether the effort is spent doing the operation the subject is made of, and difficulty is the by-product of moving that operation to the learner.
questions.stem: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?

options.A: Learning follows the effort a course demands, so a course improves as it asks for more, provided the increase is gradual enough to be borne.
options.B: A difficulty pays only where it makes the learner perform the subject’s own judgement; it is the by-product of moving that work, not the ingredient.
options.C: Students judge their own progress by how easy the work feels, so a course must teach them to distrust it first, though distrust alone teaches nothing.
options.D: A teacher should do as little in the room as possible, since whatever a class is not required to do for itself it will not learn to do at all.

explanation.expert_notice: The final paragraph states the thesis as a correction of the author's own mistake: the visitor did not make the hour harder, she moved one decision, and 'the difficulty was simply what that felt like from inside'. The sentence 'Difficulty is the symptom and not the medicine' is the passage in miniature.
explanation.correct_reasoning: The correct option keeps both halves of that correction: the condition under which a difficulty pays, and the demotion of difficulty from cause to by-product. It is also the only reading under which the audit makes sense, since it explains at once why two changes were worth keeping and why eleven identical-looking obstacles were not. The closing test — what is the student doing while spending the effort — is a restatement of the same condition.
explanation.question_type_note: In a narrative that ends in a correction, the main idea is the corrected claim, not the claim the narrator started with. Check that the statement you pick explains the passage's failures as well as its successes.
explanation.reading_habit: When a writer describes converting to a rule and then misapplying it, the thesis is the restriction that the misapplication revealed. Look for the sentence that says what the successful cases had and the failures lacked.

distractors.why_wrong: This is the conclusion the author says he drew and drew too widely, and the second and third paragraphs are the record of its failure. It also cannot accommodate the visiting lecturer, who asked for less work than he did and whose hour produced the best examination answers he had seen. The proviso about a gradual increase does not rescue it, since the audit sorts the changes by kind rather than by amount, and the one that worked best cost twenty seconds.
distractors.seductive_element: It is the lesson the opening episode appears to teach, and a reader who has fixed it in the first paragraph will find everything afterwards reading as a matter of dosage.

distractors.why_wrong: The passage's remarks about resentment and ratings are used to show that feeling is not a measure of value in either direction, not to make the management of feeling the subject. The change that worked best produced no feeling at all to distrust.
distractors.seductive_element: Complaint, falling ratings and the phrase about how difficulty felt from inside are all in the text, and they assemble easily into a thesis about self-assessment.

distractors.why_wrong: The failed year is largely a list of things the lecturer stopped doing, and it made the course worse. What the author defends is not withdrawal but the transfer of one particular kind of work, and his own counter-example is the prediction habit, which added a step rather than removing one.
distractors.seductive_element: It is the near-tie: both surviving changes involve the teacher doing less, and the maxim is a familiar one that sounds like the moral of the story.

vocabulary.meaning_here: having no effect; doing no work of its own

vocabulary.passage_use: Two of the changes survived the audit I made afterwards
vocabulary.meaning_here: a deliberate item-by-item review to see what stands up

vocabulary.passage_use: The diagnostic question is not how much effort a task costs.
vocabulary.meaning_here: serving to tell one case from another; the test that sorts them

mentor.challenge: A teacher tells you about a year in which he made everything harder and everything got worse. Watch for the moment the story stops being about how much difficulty and starts being about what kind.
mentor.one_sentence_summary: A visiting lecturer's hour, which asked for less work rather than more, taught the author that a difficulty only pays when it makes the learner perform the judgement the subject consists of, so the difficulty is a symptom of a transferred decision rather than the thing that does the teaching.
mentor.main_idea: Struggle is not what makes learning stick. What makes it stick is being made to do the thing the subject is actually made of — in this case, reaching a verdict before being shown a method. Difficulty is what that feels like, not what causes the gain, so obstacles that cost effort without requiring that work return nothing at all.
mentor.simple_explanation:
A visiting teacher took one of the author's classes. Instead of explaining first and setting a problem afterwards, she put a question up, gave four minutes, and made everyone write down an answer before she said anything. Most answers were wrong. Then she showed the working exactly as he would have. The only difference was the order. Her students did better in the exam on that topic.

He decided the lesson was that hard is good, and spent the next year making his course hard in every way he could think of: harder readings, sudden deadlines, no slides, questions about things he had not taught, blurry photocopies, a new seating plan every week. The course was definitely harder. The marks went down, and the students' opinion of it went down further.

Afterwards he went through the changes one by one. Only two were worth keeping. One was dropping the slides, which the class hated, because deciding what is worth writing down is part of what a statistician actually does. The other was something nobody even noticed: asking the class to guess the result of an example before he worked it out. It took twenty seconds.

The rest did nothing. A blurry page just takes longer to read. A moved deadline just has to be survived. A new neighbour just has to be put up with. They all made the course harder, and none of them made the students do the real work of the subject.

So his conclusion is this: the visitor had not added difficulty, she had moved a decision from her to them, and difficulty was only how that felt. 'Make it harder' is therefore the wrong instruction. And complaining is no guide either, since the change he would keep was the one they hated most, and the one that worked best was never even noticed.
mentor.why_difficult: The passage converts twice, and a reader can stop after either turn. The opening episode makes a strong case for difficulty, and a reader who leaves with it will find the failed year reading as a matter of degree. The failed year then makes a strong case against difficulty, and a reader who leaves with that will treat the piece as a recantation. The real claim lives in the third paragraph's audit, where two changes are separated from the rest that looked identical, and it depends on a distinction between effort and the operation the effort is spent on, which the passage states only once, in the clause about doing the thing the course existed to teach.
mentor.author_intention: To stop a real finding from being applied as a slogan, by showing that the same teacher, following the slogan faithfully, produced a harder course that taught less.

paragraph_journey.note: A visitor makes the class answer before she explains anything. She asks for less work, not more, and her students do better.
He concludes that hard is good and spends a year adding obstacles of every kind. Marks fall and ratings fall further.
Only two changes were worth keeping, and they are the two that made students do the subject's own work. The others just cost effort.
The visitor moved a decision rather than adding difficulty. Difficulty is the feeling that goes with the move, so complaint measures nothing.

mentor.tone_progression: Rueful and story-telling at the start, briskly self-accusing through the catalogue of the failed year, and exacting at the end, where the author stops describing what happened and states the distinction the whole account was built to support.
key_transitions: 'I drew the obvious conclusion, and drew it far too widely.' (paragraph 2) — the anecdote turns into a cautionary tale.
'Two of the changes survived the audit I made afterwards, and they are not the two anyone would pick.' (paragraph 3) — the sorting begins.
'Difficulty is the symptom and not the medicine' (paragraph 4) — the sentence the passage exists to reach.
mentor.misunderstanding: Readers build one of two wrong pictures. The first is that the author has abandoned the idea that struggle helps, which the third paragraph denies by keeping two changes and by praising the visitor's hour throughout. The second is that his mistake was excess — that a smaller dose of the same medicine would have worked — which the audit rules out, since the obstacles he abandons are not milder versions of the ones he keeps but different in kind, and one of the survivors costs twenty seconds.
mentor.traps_summary: Options here are built by dropping a restriction. The author says a transfer of work pays when it is a transfer of the subject's own judgement; distractors offer transfers of any work, effort of any kind, and discomfort of any source, each of which the failed year contains an example of. When an author's claim has a condition attached, the most attractive wrong answer is the claim with the condition removed.
mentor.reading_lesson: When a writer reports converting to a principle and then failing with it, read the failure as the place where the principle's condition is hiding. Find the sentence that says what the successful cases had that the failures lacked, and treat that sentence as the thesis, because every question about what would help, what follows, or what the piece is for will turn on it rather than on the vivid opening episode.
mentor.real_world: The same confusion runs through training at work, gym programmes and language apps, where the measurable thing is how demanding a task feels and the thing that matters is whether the demand falls on the skill you came to acquire.
mentor.takeaway: Effort is what a difficulty costs; the question is always what the effort buys.
mentor.reflection_question: In something you are trying to learn, what exactly are you doing during the hardest part of the work, and is it what you will have to do without help?
